_source.name: pstack
_source.author: Lauren Tan
_source.borrowed: The 23 principle names, and the trigger text in the `trigger` field (verbatim from each pstack SKILL.md description). The `short`, `rule`, `home` and `closest` fields are this repository's own work.
_source.note: A `home` of null means the library has no page that covers this principle. Do not cite one; say the principle is agent-conduct, argued from this index rather than from a page.

_usage: Source of truth for INDEX.md. Regenerate with: python scripts/build_index.py. A `home.anchor` must appear verbatim in `home.file` or the build fails.

principles.name: prove-it-works
principles.short: after finishing a task, before declaring done
principles.trigger: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'
principles.rule: Verify against the real artifact: run the feature, read the value, inspect the diff. Never a proxy, a self-report, or 'it compiles'.

principles.name: guard-the-context-window
principles.short: context filling up with large outputs or repeated reads
principles.trigger: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.
principles.rule: Route bulk to subagents and keep reduced findings in the main thread, never raw payloads.

principles.name: never-block-on-the-human
principles.short: tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work
principles.trigger: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.
principles.rule: On reversible work, proceed and present the result. Reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.

principles.name: build-the-lever
principles.short: non-trivial or bulk work: edits, migrations, checks
principles.trigger: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.
principles.rule: Build the tool that does the work or proves it, rather than doing bulk work by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

principles.name: encode-lessons-in-structure
principles.short: writing the same instruction a second time
principles.trigger: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.
principles.rule: A rule written twice becomes a lint, flag, check or script, not more prose.

principles.name: attack-the-premise
principles.short: two fixes sharing one premise failed the same gate
principles.trigger: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.
principles.rule: When two fixes sharing one premise fail the same gate, census which actors hold the imbalance and question the premise instead of writing a third fix that assumes it.
principles.closest: code-review-principles.html: "Review the Intent, Not Just the Implementation"

principles.name: fix-root-causes
principles.short: debugging a symptom
principles.trigger: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there; reproduce first, ask why until you reach it, resist nil-check guards that silence crashes.
principles.rule: Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there. Reproduce first, and resist the nil-check guard that only silences the crash.
principles.closest: error-handling-principles.html: "Errors Should Gain Context as They Bubble Up"

principles.name: make-operations-idempotent
principles.short: designing commands or loops that run amid crashes and retries
principles.trigger: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.
principles.rule: Commands, lifecycle steps and loops converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

principles.name: separate-before-serializing-shared-state
principles.short: concurrent actors writing the same file, branch or key
principles.trigger: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.
principles.rule: Eliminate the sharing first. Serialize only when one shared writer is a real invariant rather than a convenience.

principles.name: experience-first
principles.short: product, UX or feature-scope tradeoffs
principles.trigger: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.
principles.rule: Choose user delight over implementation convenience. Fewer polished features beat more rough ones.

principles.name: exhaust-the-design-space
principles.short: novel UI or architecture decision with no precedent
principles.trigger: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.
principles.rule: With no precedent in the codebase, build two or three competing prototypes and compare them side by side before committing.

principles.name: foundational-thinking
principles.short: before writing logic: core types, data structures, ordering
principles.trigger: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.
principles.rule: Get the core types and data structures right before the logic. Downstream code should then be obvious.

principles.name: laziness-protocol
principles.short: refactoring, sizing a diff, tempted to add a layer
principles.trigger: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
principles.rule: Bias to deletion, and to the smallest change that solves the problem. If a maintainer would find it exhausting, it is the wrong solution.

principles.name: subtract-before-you-add
principles.short: sequencing an addition, refactor or rewrite
principles.trigger: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.
principles.rule: Remove dead code, redundant validators and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

home.anchor: Leave the Code Cleaner Than You Found It

principles.name: minimize-reader-load
principles.short: code that is hard to trace, or shaping code for a reader
principles.trigger: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.
principles.rule: Count the layers between question and answer, and the hidden state in a reader's head. Collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

home.anchor: Clarity Is More Important Than Brevity

principles.name: model-the-domain
principles.short: stateful logic, heavy branching, a shape repeated across files
principles.trigger: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals.
principles.rule: Encode the domain in a structure instead of repeating a shape assumption as scattered conditionals.

home.anchor: Name for the Domain — Not the Implementation

principles.name: boundary-discipline
principles.short: wiring validation, error handling or a framework adapter
principles.trigger: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.
principles.rule: Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs). Trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

home.anchor: Detect Errors at the Boundary — Not Deep in the Logic

principles.name: type-system-discipline
principles.short: designing types or reviewing a signature in a typed language
principles.trigger: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, refuse to lie to the compiler, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.
principles.rule: Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, and never lie to the compiler.

home.anchor: Errors Are Types — Give Them Structure

principles.name: test-behavior-not-implementation
principles.short: writing, changing or keeping a test
principles.trigger: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result they observe against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns undefined, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.
principles.rule: Call the code the way its users do and assert the observed result against a literal. If it passes when every import returns undefined, rewrite or delete it.

principles.name: sequence-verifiable-units
principles.short: multi-step work, and how commits or PRs are stacked
principles.trigger: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.
principles.rule: Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

principles.name: migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
principles.short: introducing a new internal API while old callers exist
principles.trigger: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.
principles.rule: Migrate the callers and delete the old API in the same wave. Do not keep a compatibility layer alive.

principles.name: outcome-oriented-execution
principles.short: planned rewrites with explicit phase boundaries
principles.trigger: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.
principles.rule: Converge on the target architecture. Do not spend effort preserving a smooth intermediate state.

principles.name: redesign-from-first-principles
principles.short: integrating a new requirement into an existing design
principles.trigger: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.
principles.rule: Redesign as if the new requirement had been a day-one assumption, instead of bolting it onto the current shape.

home.anchor: Start Simple — The Monolith Is Not a Mistake
